Hi Avery —

Thanks again for taking the time earlier. To get our implementation team going I need a short set of usage numbers so we can recommend a model shortlist and a capacity baseline (hosted vs Dedicated). Can you confirm the following for the initial rollout (first 3 months):

- Avg daily active users (DAU) or API callers and expected growth cadence
- Typical prompt length (tokens) and typical generated completion length (tokens)
- Peak concurrent sessions or concurrent live inference requests at peak hour
- Any explicit context length requirements (examples: full patient note history up to X tokens)
- Latency SLO (p95 / p99) and any processing constraints (PII handling, on-prem requirement)

If it's easier, attach a short token/profile CSV — we'll consume it to produce a short sizing spreadsheet.

I'm cc'ing Monica (implementation lead) and Laura (solutions) to keep them looped.

Thanks — goal is a one-page recommended model shortlist + a cost/throughput sketch by Monday.

Best,

Hi Ben —

Appreciate the quick follow. Numbers below reflect our expected Phase 1 (pilot, 3 months):

- DAU / API callers: ~3,000 unique clinicians (internal users) but only ~600 active on any given day answering triage/support workflows. We expect steady growth to ~1,200 active/day by month 3.
- Prompt length: typically structured data + short note, ~90–150 tokens (we see 120 tokens avg)
- Completion length: guidance and suggested phrasing, ~200–600 tokens (avg 420 tokens)
- Context needs: we need to surface up to two prior visit notes plus a short problem list — worst-case ~3,500 tokens. So safe context length is 4k tokens, but some internal docs may push to 6k; we can truncate non-critical fields.
- Peak concurrency: during morning rounds we expect spikes up to ~25 concurrent inference sessions (each session may generate a back-and-forth, but concurrency for generation peaks around 25–30).
- Latency: clinicians want snappy replies — target p95 under 600ms; p99 under 1.5s is tolerable in pilot.
- Compliance: PHI/PII — data remains in our cloud (AWS). We need SOC2 evidence and an option for VPC/private deployment later.

Attached is a small token profile (CSV) and a sample prompt set to help sizing. Also looping in Rajesh (procurement) for SOW/contract questions.

Thanks,
Avery Collins
Director, Digital Care Experience
SummitCare

Attachments: summitcare_token_profile.csv, prototype_prompt_set.md

Subject: Re: SummitCare onboarding: model fit and throughput estimate — recommended shortlist and sizing sketch

Ben/Avery/Laura —

Quick model shortlist + sizing sketch for the pilot based on the CSV and prompt set. I kept the recommendation pragmatic: prioritize accuracy and context over lowest cost for pilot, then optimize.

1) Candidate models (pilot order of preference)
- open-13B-chat (quantized 8-bit) — Pros: strong instruction-following, good for clinical phrasing; supports 8k context comfortably when run on 80GB-class GPUs with KV cache optimizations. Estimated latency (single request, no batching) ~350–500ms p95 at 2 tokens/sec generation depending on hardware; with dynamic batching p95 can approach your 600ms goal for 420-token completions on Dedicated.
- mixtral-8x-ish (7–8B class) — Pros: good cost/latency balance; suitable as fallback for throughput-heavy windows. Supports 8k context in trimmed mode; performance on quantized runtimes is very strong.
- small-accelerated (4–6B quantized) — Pros: lowest cost for simple prompt/template completions; recommended for non-critical routing (e.g., canned templates). Not recommended for full clinical summarization.

2) Context and token budgeting assumptions
- Pilot daily tokens (est): 600 active/day * (120 prompt + 420 completion) * 30 sessions/day average = ~0.9–1.1M tokens/day. Allow 20% headroom -> 1.2–1.3M tokens/day.
- Peak hour concurrency sizing: assume 30 concurrent generation requests with average completion 420 tokens -> sustained token-per-second during peak ~ (30 * 420) / average_generation_window (~2.5s) -> ~5k tokens/s (rough sketch). This maps to roughly 1–2 high-end GPUs (H100/A100) if you target low-latency 8k-context runs with quantization; if you accept higher p95 latency, you can multiplex more on fewer GPUs.

3) Deployment recommendation
- Short term: Hosted trial using open-13B-chat quantized — quick onboarding, Redwood-managed; gives baseline for quality and lets us instrument real token profiles.
- Medium term (if they need consistent p95 & data isolation): Redwood Dedicated with 2x80GB GPUs (start 1 node with 2 GPUs) + autoscale to 3 GPUs for morning spikes. Dedicated gives predictable latency, direct capacity planning, and private network peering for improved compliance posture.

4) Next steps from Redwood (deliverables)
- One-page model shortlist + cost sketch (this email)
- Sizing workbook (we'll convert the attached CSV into a token-by-route tab) — ETA Monday EOD
- Draft SOW + pricing for Hosted trial and Dedicated baseline — I'll prepare a first-pass SOW for Ben to share with Rajesh/Procurement.

Notes/risks:
- If SummitCare needs full 6k+ context for many requests, cost and latency increase materially; we should limit longest history to critical fields or consider sharded retrieval + context stitching.
- SOC2 evidence and VPC options available; privacy review will be needed before production.

I'll prepare the sizing workbook and SOW draft — flagging the Dedicated 2x80GB baseline for cost calc.

Thanks,
Monica Patel
Implementation Lead, Redwood Inference

A) Hosted trial (30 days) — open-13B-chat quantized, usage billing per token, soft SLA, Redwood-managed.
B) Dedicated baseline — 1 node (2x80GB GPUs) with autoscale policy to +1 GPU for 2-hour morning window, monthly committed capacity pricing; includes VPC peering option and SOC2 evidence pack.

Please review the attached SOW-draft.pdf and the CSV. Rajesh — happy to hop on a quick call to walk through pricing and procurement items; if Procurement needs redlines, send them back and we'll route to Legal.
